subject: Chronos: temporary SLA relief + traffic fencing request for modelv2b latency variance
messages:
From: Ari Bolton <ari@chronos.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@chronos.ai
Date: Fri, 24 May 2029 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 jump after model switch to modelv2b — data and graphs attached

Monica / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp p95 latency increase and a higher tail error rate since we moved 30% of production traffic to modelv2b at ~11:30 PDT today. Baseline p95 was ~210ms, after the switch it's spiking to ~950ms for a subset of queries. We attached graphs and a short sample of error traces. This is affecting two endpoints (chat and completion) — our customers in APAC are timing out.

Can you confirm whether this is an expected degradation for v2b (quantization profile differences), or whether something has regressed on the inference side? We need a mitigation plan — if there's a way to pin to the previous variant for our account while you investigate, that would help prevent SLA breaches on our end.

Thanks,
Ari Bolton
Head of Product
Chronos AI

Attachments: chronos_latency_graphs_may24.png, chronos_error_samples_log.txt
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Bolton <ari@chronos.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 May 2029 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump after model switch to modelv2b — data and graphs attached

Hi Ari — thanks for the quick signal and the attachments. We're pulling logs and tracing now.

Immediate options we can take while we investigate:
- Pin Chronos traffic to the previous model variant (modelv2a) for your account only.
- Apply a temporary rate cap on high-concurrency flows to reduce queuing (traffic fencing) for your routed requests.
- Activate a limited SLA relief window (provisional) while we run a canary rollback and diagnostic.

I need authorization internally to enact per-account pinning + a provisional SLA carveout for up to 48 hours. Ben/Hannah/Karthik: could you comment on risk/effort for pin + traffic fencing and whether we can approve provisional SLA relief (credits/contract impact) for Chronos?

Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 May 2029 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump after model switch to modelv2b — data and graphs attached

Monica — from an ops standpoint pinning Chronos to v2a for a single account is straightforward (route rule + variant pin). Low risk. Traffic fencing (per-account rate limits / burst smoothing) is also available and can be applied immediately; it will reduce peak throughput and may temporarily raise latency for larger batched requests but should stop the p95 breaches.

Regarding provisional SLA relief: we usually offer a short window (24-48 hrs) for incidents caused by platform rollouts, with a credit estimate tied to incoming token volume. I'll need approval from revenue ops for any credit > $5k. Recommend offering a provisional 30% credit cap with a promise to re-evaluate after diagnostics — it both protects the customer standing and limits financial exposure.

I can push the pin + fencing once Hannah okays from reliability side.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 May 2029 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump after model switch to modelv2b — data and graphs attached

Acknowledged. I'm running the canary rollback plan on a dry run now. Quick notes:
- We saw an increase in decode GPU stalls with modelv2b on sequence lengths > 512 — possible kernel path regression tied to the new attention kernel.
- Pinning to v2a should restore latency to baseline quickly. We'll validate with a 5% canary and escalate to full pin if green.
- Traffic fencing is a good short-term control to avoid cascading queue growth; implement a token-rate cap and a burst-window of 2s.

Monica: approve the provisional SLA relief messaging and credit cap (Ben suggested 30%) so I can proceed to activate the pin and fencing for Chronos. I will include rollback steps and postmortem owners in the change request doc.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Reliability Engineering
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Bolton <ari@chronos.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@chronos.ai
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump after model switch to modelv2b — data and graphs attached

Ari — quick update and authorization:

We've approved a provisional SLA relief window for Chronos (24 hours, automatically re-evaluated) and will cap on-account credits at 30% for the incident window, pending final revenue-ops sign-off.

Actions we're taking now (ETA in parentheses):
- Pin Chronos account to modelv2a (per-account routing) — activation in 5m.
- Apply traffic fencing: token-rate cap + 2s burst smoothing — immediate.
- Run targeted canary rollback for v2b with telemetry watch (Hannah) — starting now.
- We will generate a service change request and postmortem link after stabilization.

Can procurement confirm the contract clause for SLA credits so we can proceed without a signed amendment? If Chronos prefers a formal SOW addendum, we can draft during the stabilization window.

Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: service_change_request_chronos.docx
From: Ari Bolton <ari@chronos.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump after model switch to modelv2b — data and graphs attached

Team — thank you, that plan sounds good and appreciated. Procurement confirms the master services agreement allows provisional credits for platform-caused regressions; they'll follow up with the specific contract reference early next week.

We're observing immediate improvement after pin + fencing (p95 returning to ~230ms). Please proceed with the canary diagnostics and let us know if you see residual regressions on specific query shapes — we've shared an example corpus in the error_samples log. We'll await the postmortem and the SLO-credit estimate.

—Ari
